title: Studies for the optimization of measurement protocols
summary:
To ensure excellent quality of MRI studies in the medical school, continuous adaptation and improvement of MRI sequences is necessary. Human MRI research is highly dependent on high quality equipment and optimal sequence parameters adjusted by specialized MR physicists. 
The present study compares different MR measurement protocols. Simple paradigms with sensory stimulation serve as a reference. In the future, this will allow fMRI studies to be more efficient. The requested screening and pilot study protocol will allow us to provide optimized sequences for different specific anatomical brain regions by measuring 100 healthy volunteers. This protocol will serve us for screening and pilot studies, which will be the basis for further fMRI studies, where optimal measurement sequences should be guaranteed.

interventions.name: During the different screening and pilot study approaches in healthy subjects, the order of presentation of the respective sensory stimuli is systematically varied to minimize bias. Due to the exploratory nature, no systematic randomization is necessary.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible subjects aged 18 to 70 years, representing the local population.
Exclusion criteria:
- in women: Pregnancy and lactation
- active implants (e.g. pacemakers, drug pumps, etc.) 
- metal parts (e.g. screws after bone fracture)
- claustrophobia
- severe back pain
- very large tattoos (altogether more than would fit on a DIN-A-4 sheet) and tattoos on the face
- Symptoms of Covid-19
